_about: Hand-written reasoning for each study session: how the conclusion follows from the numbers, step by step, in plain words. Written by reading each session's results; load-sessions.js attaches it by session id. Update it by hand if the analysis changes.

mcd-1020.conclusion: Nothing abnormal. Your heart and temperature were normal at rest, and the changes after exercise were the expected ones.

steps.found: 83 beats a minute. The normal adult range at rest is 50–100.
steps.so: Normal. It sits in the upper half of the range, which is common in young adults.

steps.found: 36.7 °C estimated core temperature. Fever starts at 38.0 °C.
steps.so: Normal, no sign of fever.

steps.found: Heart rate rose by 17 to 100 beats a minute. The beat-to-beat variation fell from 28 to 9 ms, and muscle tension rose from 0.28 to 0.46.
steps.so: This is how a healthy body responds to effort: the heart speeds up and becomes more regular, and muscles stay a little tense. It is not a problem.

steps.look: Can the camera reading be trusted?
steps.found: The camera measured 73 at rest while the heart sensor measured 83 — 10 beats apart. After exercise they were 23 apart. The camera signal was weak (2.3 dB).
steps.so: The camera was not accurate for you in this sitting, so the heart sensor's number was used instead. This is why the station has a backup sensor.

steps.found: Both main readings — heart rate and temperature — are inside their normal ranges. The only issue was with the camera, not with you.
steps.so: No need to see a doctor. Note: the heart, temperature and muscle readings in this prototype are simulated from your recorded vitals.

mcd-1149.conclusion: Nothing abnormal at rest. Your heart rate did not rise after exercise, most likely because the exercise was light — one sitting is not enough to say more.

steps.found: 75 beats a minute. The normal adult range at rest is 50–100.
steps.so: Normal.

steps.found: 36.5 °C estimated core temperature. Fever starts at 38.0 °C.
steps.so: Normal, no sign of fever.

steps.found: Heart rate stayed at 75 — no rise at all. Usually it goes up after effort.
steps.so: On its own this looks unusual, so we checked the other signals before deciding what it means.

steps.look: Did the body respond in other ways?
steps.found: Yes. The beat-to-beat variation fell by half (26 → 13 ms) and muscle tension doubled (0.25 → 0.54).
steps.so: The body did react to the exercise. A steady heart rate with these changes fits a light bout of exercise better than a heart problem.

steps.look: Can the camera reading be trusted?
steps.found: The camera was within 4 beats of the heart sensor at rest, with a clear signal.
steps.so: Yes — the camera alone would have given the right answer.

steps.found: All resting readings are normal. The flat heart rate after exercise has a likely harmless explanation, but this is one short recording.
steps.so: No need to see a doctor for this result. If you notice you get breathless or tired easily with effort, mention it at your next routine check-up. Note: the heart, temperature and muscle readings in this prototype are simulated from your recorded vitals.

mcd-1217.conclusion: Nothing abnormal. Your heart rate and temperature were both normal, and the camera reading agreed with the heart sensor.

steps.found: 69 beats a minute. The normal adult range at rest is 50–100.
steps.so: Normal, near the middle of the range.

steps.found: 36.5 °C estimated core temperature. Fever starts at 38.0 °C.
steps.so: Normal, no sign of fever.

steps.found: 32 ms at rest. Below 20 ms is considered low.
steps.so: Healthy — your heart adjusts normally from beat to beat.

steps.look: Can the camera reading be trusted?
steps.found: The camera measured 63, the heart sensor 69 — 6 beats apart, with a strong, clear signal (12.3 dB).
steps.so: Yes. The contactless reading was good enough on its own.

steps.found: Every reading is inside its normal range and the two heart measurements agree.
steps.so: No need to see a doctor. Note: the heart, temperature and muscle readings in this prototype are simulated from your recorded vitals.

drivedb-drive05.conclusion: Nothing abnormal. The signals were flagged because they changed a lot while driving, but those changes are the body's normal reaction to city traffic.

steps.found: 66 beats a minute. The normal adult range at rest is 50–100.
steps.so: Normal.

steps.found: 63 ms. Below 20 ms is considered low.
steps.so: Healthy and relaxed.

steps.look: Why were all three signals flagged?
steps.found: While driving in the city, heart rate rose to 90 (+24), beat-to-beat variation halved (63 → 31 ms) and muscle tension rose about 25 times.
steps.so: The flags mean 'this changed a lot from rest', not 'this is unhealthy'. All three moved in the same direction at the same time.

steps.found: A faster heart, less beat-to-beat variation and tense muscles together are the classic pattern of short-term stress. The person was driving through city traffic.
steps.so: The changes are explained by the activity. Even while driving, heart rate (90) stayed under 100.

steps.found: The resting readings are normal, and the driving readings show a normal stress response.
steps.so: No need to see a doctor. This recording shows how the body reacts to stress, not a health problem.

thermal-s01.conclusion: No health conclusion can be drawn from this recording. It shows what drinking something cold does to face temperatures.

steps.found: Only a thermal camera, before, during and after drinking a cold drink. There is no heart sensor, and the temperatures were rebuilt from the colours of the thermal image.
steps.so: We can compare regions of the face with each other, but the exact temperatures are not reliable enough for a medical reading.

steps.found: The mouth cooled by 1.35 °C, the eyes by 0.64 °C and the forehead by 0.49 °C, and the nose warmed by 0.65 °C. Afterwards the mouth returned almost to where it started (33.9 °C vs 34.0 °C).
steps.so: The cold drink cooled the mouth most. The change went away afterwards, as expected.

steps.found: The pattern is explained by the drink, not by the person's health, and there are no reliable vital signs to check.
steps.so: Not assessable. This session is here to show how the thermal camera sees changes on the face.
